# BSCS Teaching & Learning

Public teaching guidance for Bradley Stoke Community School staff. EEF evidence snapshot checked August 2026. Research evidence, BSCS agreed practice and practitioner guidance are kept distinct. Each strategy page states its evidence rating.

## Home
- [Home](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/): Explore and implement evidence-informed teaching strategies that fit the BSCS teaching model, and use them for Individual Development CPD.

## Strategy

- [Variation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/strategies/variation/): Changing examples to deepen understanding. Use variation to help students notice the structure of an idea rather than copy surface features.

- [Wait time](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/strategies/wait-time/): Giving everyone time to think. Use wait time to give everyone a chance to retrieve, reason and prepare an answer. Include a pause after a st

- [Circulation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/strategies/circulation/): Sampling independent work and responding. Use circulation to read learning across the room, identify the exact error and choose a response.

- [Precorrections](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/strategies/precorrections/): Preventing predictable problems before they start. Use a precorrection when a predictable situation repeatedly produces the same difficulty.

- [Oracy for learning](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/strategies/oracy-for-learning/): Teaching speaking and listening explicitly. Use oracy routines to teach speaking and listening as skills that support disciplinary thinking.

## Pupil need
- [Pupils forget what they have been taught](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/forgetting/): Pupils can answer soon after teaching but struggle weeks later, or start new topics without the knowledge they need. Forgetting is normal. R
- [Only a few pupils answer questions](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/participation/): The same hands go up, quieter pupils rarely contribute, and you are not sure the rest of the class is thinking. Make thinking everyone's job
- [I can't tell who has understood](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/checking/): Answers from a few pupils leave you unsure whether the class is ready to move on, and errors surface later in independent work. Collect evid
- [Pupils struggle when working independently](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/independence/): Pupils seem to follow the model but make many errors, stall or ask for help as soon as they work alone. Independence is built in stages. Sho
- [Pupils don't follow my explanations](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/explanations/): Explanations feel clear to you, but pupils lose the thread, cannot repeat the key idea or need it explained again. Reduce what pupils have t
- [Pupils keep making the same mistakes](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/misconceptions/): The same errors recur across lessons and assessments, even after you have corrected them. Plan for the misconception before the lesson, expo
- [Learning time is lost at the start, transitions or end](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/routines/): Lessons start slowly, attention drifts during instructions and transitions take longer than they should. Consistent, rehearsed routines prot
- [Pupils' answers are short or imprecise](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/precision/): Answers are one word, vague or partly correct, and pupils rarely use subject vocabulary accurately. Raise the expectation of what a complete
- [Some pupils can't access the task, or need more challenge](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/access/): The same task leaves some pupils stuck and others finished early, and adaptations risk lowering the goal. Keep the goal ambitious for everyo
- [Feedback isn't improving pupils' work](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/needs/feedback/): You spend time giving feedback, but the same issues reappear and pupils don't use the comments. Feedback works when pupils act on it. Focus 

## BSCS agreed practice
- [Our model](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/): Plan deliberately, protect attention and make thinking visible. The model supports professional judgement across subjects and phases.
- [Lesson preparation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/lesson-preparation/): Plan from the learning goal, anticipate barriers and decide how pupils will think.
- [Climate & Culture](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/climate-culture/): Build warm relationships and consistent routines that protect attention.
- [Drive Thinking for All](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/drive-thinking/): Give every pupil time to think, contribute and explain their reasoning.
- [Check & Adapt](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/check-adapt/): Gather useful evidence, choose a response and check again.
- [Do Now](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/do-now/): Start calmly with independent retrieval and purposeful review.
- [Explain](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/explain/): Make new knowledge clear through small steps and expert modelling.
- [Secure learning through practice](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/practice/): Move from guided rehearsal to confident independent performance.
- [Feedback to improve](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/feedback/): Make feedback precise and give pupils time to act on it.
- [Feedback principles at BSCS](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/model/feedback-principles/): At BSCS, effective feedback is underpinned by the following principles:
- [Entry and Do Now](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/routines/entry/): 1. Before students enter the classroom, the teacher ensures that the Do Now is visible and ready. Students use calm waiting if the teacher i
- [Signalling for attention and giving instructions](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/routines/attention/): Prime students before the transition
- [Exit routine](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/routines/exit/): Teacher ends learning before explaining logistics

## Individual Development
- [Individual Development](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/develop/): Use this site to choose, try and refine one change to your classroom practice.
- [Writing a precise goal](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/develop/writing-your-goal/): Turn a broad aim into one observable change: I will … so that students …
- [Developmental peer observation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/develop/peer-observation/): A short, focused protocol for observing one change and how pupils respond.
- [Evaluating impact and deciding what next](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/develop/evaluating-impact/): Separate how well you implemented the change from its effect on pupils, then refine, embed or rethink.

## Practitioner profile
- [Activating prior knowledge](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/activating-prior-knowledge/): Bringing the specific existing knowledge needed for new learning into working memory and making the connection explicit.
- [Adaptive teaching: anticipate, assess, respond and monitor](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/adaptive-teaching-cycle/): Start from what pupils need to learn. Identify prerequisite knowledge, likely misconceptions and barriers to access before the lesson. Plan 
- [Adaptive teaching: high challenge, responsive support](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/adaptive-teaching-high-challenge-responsive-support/): Maintaining a shared ambitious goal while adjusting explanation, representation, scaffolding, grouping, time or practice in response to barr
- [Annotated seating plans and purposeful adult deployment](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/annotated-seating-plans-and-purposeful-adult-deployment/): Using current knowledge of pupils to position students and adults deliberately, annotate practical supports, plan talk partners and define c
- [Backwards planning / Begin with the end](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/backwards-planning-begin-with-the-end/): Planning from the intended curriculum outcome or performance and working backwards to the prerequisite knowledge, intermediate steps, practi
- [Call and response / Choral response](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/call-and-response-choral-response/): A clearly cued routine in which the whole class gives the same concise response in unison.
- [Checking for understanding / TAPPLE](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/checking-for-understanding-tapple/): A continuous feedback loop in which teachers ask, pause, select a response method, listen or look, interpret the evidence and act.
- [Checks for listening](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/checks-for-listening/): Brief, planned prompts that require students to reproduce, reframe or act on what has just been said, showing whether attention became usabl
- [Circulation and actionable live feedback](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/circulation-and-actionable-live-feedback/): Purposeful movement through a planned route to scan, read, compare work with criteria and give brief feedback that prompts immediate improve
- [Close the feedback loop: Own and Track](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/close-the-feedback-loop-own-and-track/): Ensuring students record the accurate answer, understand why it is accurate and visibly amend, annotate, redraft or re-practise their own wo
- [Cognitive simplicity in slides and resources](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/cognitive-simplicity-in-slides-and-resources/): Designing explanations and materials so attention is directed to essential information: removing clutter, keeping related information togeth
- [Cold calling](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/cold-calling/): Asking the question to the whole class, allowing thinking time and then warmly inviting a selected student to respond.
- [Do Now: retrieval-rich lesson start](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/do-now-retrieval-rich-lesson-start/): A short, immediately accessible and independently completed start-of-lesson routine, usually built around spaced retrieval rather than new c
- [Everybody Writes and accountable discussion](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/everybody-writes-and-accountable-discussion/): Using brief individual writing before or after talk so every student develops, records and revises an idea.
- [Everyone, Together, Anyone (ETA) and active participation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/everyone-together-anyone-eta-and-active-participation/): A participation framework that moves between responses from everyone, structured thinking with a partner and individual accountability.
- [Examples, non-examples and variation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/examples-non-examples-and-variation/): Choosing positive examples, near-miss non-examples and deliberately varied cases to reveal the defining features and boundaries of a concept
- [Exit tickets and retrieval quizzes](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/exit-tickets-and-retrieval-quizzes/): Brief independent end-of-lesson or cumulative questions designed for rapid analysis and a clear instructional follow-up.
- [Explicit vocabulary instruction with active practice](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/explicit-vocabulary-instruction-with-active-practice/): Teaching a word's meaning, pronunciation, form, examples, non-examples and connections, followed by repeated retrieval and use in context.
- [Fading support and backward fading](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/fading-support-and-backward-fading/): Reducing a model or scaffold in small evidence-led steps, often removing the final step first while keeping the task and method stable.
- [Feedback as detective work](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/feedback-as-detective-work/): Diagnosing the underlying cause of a response before deciding what information, prompt, model or practice will move learning forward.
- [Guided practice](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/guided-practice/): Short supported rehearsal in which the teacher and students co-work examples, make responses visible and correct errors before independent r
- [Hinge questions](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/hinge-questions/): A pre-planned diagnostic question at a critical point where the class response determines whether teaching moves on, consolidates or reteach
- [Least-intrusive correction and behavioural leadership](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/least-intrusive-correction-and-behavioural-leadership/): A calm graduated response that starts with visibility, proximity or non-verbal cues and escalates only as needed while preserving dignity an
- [Making participation safe](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/making-participation-safe/): Designing predictable, high-success participation in which students can think, speak, practise and make mistakes without humiliation while e
- [Mini-whiteboards for diagnosis](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/mini-whiteboards-for-diagnosis/): Using standardised, simultaneous board responses to gather valid whole-class data quickly enough to adapt in the moment.
- [Mini-whiteboards for participation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/mini-whiteboards-for-participation/): A routine in which every student commits a short written, symbolic or multiple-choice response and reveals it on a common cue.
- [Plan the exemplar and plan the error](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/plan-the-exemplar-and-plan-the-error/): Preparing a high-quality model response and the misconceptions, weak examples or incorrect processes most likely to occur.
- [Plan the explanation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/plan-the-explanation/): Deliberately scripting the conceptual route, key language, examples, representations, misconceptions and stopping points before teaching new
- [Plan the means of participation / Double plan](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/plan-the-means-of-participation-double-plan/): Planning both teacher actions and the cognitive actions students will take: thinking, retrieving, writing, discussing, explaining and revisi
- [Positive narration, precise praise and motivation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/positive-narration-precise-praise-and-motivation/): Reinforcing the actions, effort, quality and norms that support learning while building belonging, competence and value.
- [Practice for fluency, cumulative review and challenge](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/practice-for-fluency-cumulative-review-and-challenge/): Sequencing repeated, varied and spaced opportunities so accurate knowledge or processes become increasingly fluent and can be applied in mor
- [Precise individual feedback](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/precise-individual-feedback/): Brief information that identifies the exact gap and prompts the student to retrieve, correct, practise or improve while the work is still ac
- [Process questions and equitable follow-up](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/process-questions-and-equitable-follow-up/): Questions that probe how or why an answer was produced, ask for evidence, comparison or connection, and refine responses for precision.
- [Purposeful independent practice](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/purposeful-independent-practice/): Independent rehearsal and application of explicitly taught knowledge or skills, designed for accuracy, fluency and increasing automaticity.
- [Responsive micro-decisions](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/responsive-micro-decisions/): A disciplined noticing-interpreting-responding cycle that asks whether understanding is secure, where the gap lies, whether to stay or pivot
- [Responsive thresholds and high success](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/responsive-thresholds-and-high-success/): Using approximate success bands to choose a proportionate response while keeping practice in a productive zone, commonly around 80% success.
- [Retrieval practice: spacing, challenge and feedback](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/retrieval-practice-spacing-challenge-and-feedback/): Effortfully recalling previously taught knowledge after some forgetting, with low stakes and feedback that makes the retrieval event itself 
- [Routines, transitions and precorrections](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/routines-transitions-and-precorrections/): Teaching repeated classroom processes explicitly and priming students immediately before predictable difficulty points.
- [Scaffolding difficult tasks](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/scaffolding-difficult-tasks/): Temporary support such as a model, worked example, prompt, sentence stem, vocabulary bank, partial task or visual cue that preserves the amb
- [Second Chance / No Opt Out](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/second-chance-no-opt-out/): Returning to a student who could not initially answer after giving them time and access to peer responses, so that they still complete an in
- [Signal for attention and habits of attention](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/signal-for-attention-and-habits-of-attention/): A consistent cue followed by observable, inclusive attention behaviours that prepare students to listen, look or think about the intended co
- [Small steps and precise explanation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/small-steps-and-precise-explanation/): Breaking complex content into coherent, cumulative units and explaining each with concise, accurate language before immediate guided practic
- [Solid entry routines and threshold](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/solid-entry-routines-and-threshold/): A short, explicitly taught sequence for moving from corridor to classroom and beginning independent learning immediately.
- [Storytelling, analogies and memorable explanation](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/storytelling-analogies-and-memorable-explanation/): Using a concise narrative, analogy or metaphor to organise causal relationships and make an abstract idea easier to understand and remember.
- [Structured peer feedback](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/structured-peer-feedback/): Students use clear criteria and modelled language to identify a specific strength and an actionable improvement in a peer's work.
- [Thinking aloud](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/thinking-aloud/): Verbalising the expert's internal decisions, monitoring and self-correction while completing a task.
- [Turn and Talk / Think-Pair-Share / Oracy](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/turn-and-talk-think-pair-share-oracy/): Structured talk that begins with individual thinking, uses a focused paired exchange and ends with accountable sharing, writing or recheckin
- [Visualiser, live drawing and dual coding](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/visualiser-live-drawing-and-dual-coding/): Constructing writing, annotation, diagrams or models live while directing attention and revealing the decisions behind the representation.
- [Wait time](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/wait-time/): A deliberate pause after a question and a second pause after a student's response before the teacher evaluates or moves on.
- [Whole-class feedback and Show Call](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/whole-class-feedback-and-show-call/): Reviewing a set of work to identify patterns, then teaching from common strengths, misconceptions and strategically selected examples rather
- [Worked examples and providing models](https://teachinglearningedu-dotcom.github.io/reference/worked-examples-and-providing-models/): Showing a complete or partially completed solution or product, with the structure, sequence and decisions made explicit before students perf
